title: Kanayi's 'Victims' unveiled amid protest over Speaker's absence; Kasaragod's neglect takes centre stage
content: Kasaragod: The unveiling of 'Victims' -- master sculptor Kanayi Kunhiraman's tribute to the lives devastated by the endosulfan tragedy -- turned into an impromptu protest on Friday, after Assembly Speaker Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan, who was scheduled to unveil the sculpture, withdrew at the last minute. The disappointment quickly spilt over into anger, with artists, art critics and public representatives questioning not just the absence of the Speaker but what they saw as yet another instance of Kasaragod being treated as a back-of-beyond place. The district has long complained of being overlooked by successive governments. Standing 40 feet tall, 'Victims' is among the most ambitious works of Kanayi, who spent years completing the sculpture despite his advanced age. Drawing on the cubist style, the monumental sculpture depicts two children with oversized heads clinging desperately to their mother, who is facing the District Panchayat Office and seeking help. Yet, even on the day it was finally unveiled, the memorial became the centre of another painful reminder of the district's perceived neglect. Artists and art lovers had travelled from different parts of Kerala, expecting a dignified unveiling ceremony at 9.30 am. They learnt only after reaching the venue that Speaker Thiruvanchur would not be attending. District Panchayat president Sabu Abraham proposed the name of Kasaragod MP Rajmohan Unnithan as an alternative. But the artists were unwilling to accept the last-minute change, insisting that nobody other than Kanayi should unveil his own creation. Documentary filmmaker and art historian A T Mohandas, whose documentary on Kanayi's work was scheduled to be screened after the unveiling, snapped the ceremonial ribbon in protest. The ribbon was later tied back, and Kanayi himself cut it to formally unveil the sculpture. "Artists, art lovers and many others who respect Kanayi's work had gathered here from different parts of Kerala. We had travelled all this way expecting the Speaker to unveil the sculpture. It was only after reaching here that we learnt he would not be attending. Worse, the authorities could not even tell us who would unveil it in his place. That was when we began a small protest to register our anguish and disappointment," Mohandas said. He said 'Victims' deserved to be etched into the collective consciousness of Kasaragod, given what it represented. "This sculpture is dedicated to the memory of those who lost their lives, the children whose lives were cut short, and those whose health and longevity were stolen by the aerial spraying of the endosulfan pesticide. For the unveiling of such a sculpture to be reduced to this helpless situation, with nobody even able to say who would perform the ceremony, is an absurdity," he said. Kanhangad-based artist Shyamasasi said the failure to give the sculpture a proper inauguration was an embarrassment to the artistic community. "Renowned sculptor Kanayi Kunhiraman's 'Victims' is a landmark work for Kasaragod district. It is deeply disappointing that a sculpture completed after years of dedication and sacrifice, with Kanayi putting in tremendous effort even at his advanced age, should be left without a proper unveiling ceremony. What will society think of us? When we are honouring an artist of such stature and celebrating his work, for the occasion to end up without even a formal unveiling is an embarrassment to the entire artistic community," he said. The absence of ministers also came under criticism. Manjeshwar MLA and Muslim League leader A K M Ashraf did not pull his punches either. "It is deeply disappointing that we could not get a single minister to attend such an important programme organised to honour a personality like Kanayi Kunhiraman. In fact, this is something we repeatedly experience in Kasaragod. Whether it is a government led by the Left or the UDF, the attitude towards Kasaragod seems to remain the same," he said...
